# Gabrielle Sorresso {.site-name}

*PhD Candidate, Cornell Jeb E. Brooks School of Public Policy*

:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-8 .bio-block}

Hi, I'm Gabrielle — a 5th-year PhD candidate at the Cornell Jeb E. Brooks School of Public Policy. I'm an applied microeconomist studying health economics and gender. I use causal inference methods and large-scale administrative data, primarily healthcare claims, to examine how policy shapes maternal and infant health, fertility, and physician behavior.

I'm currently working on projects examining the *Dobbs* decision and its impacts on maternal and infant health and fertility, work recently recognized with the [Horowitz Foundation's Most Outstanding Project Award](https://publicpolicy.cornell.edu/news/brooks-phd-student-earns-horowitz-foundations-most-outstanding-project-award/). I also have joint work with [Colleen Carey](https://sites.google.com/site/colleenmariecarey/) and [Amanda Agan](https://sites.google.com/site/amandayagan/) on how state medical board disciplinary policy shapes physicians' future provision of care, and with [Sharon Sassler](https://www.human.cornell.edu/people/ss589) on gender wage gaps and spousal occupation.
